summary: Tested new Back/Home nav controls on /luxury-next, /communities-next, /visual-agent-demo-next, /about-next. Rendering, layout, and Home link all pass. Back button has a CRITICAL click-interception bug: the mobile-nav checkbox <input.hn-nav__toggle id='hn-nav-toggle'> overlays the header area including the Back button, so real mouse clicks never reach it (URL does not change). The Home link is unaffected because clicks land on inner SPAN/A. Also verified mobile 390px layout (icon-only, no overflow) and desktop 1920px (labels visible, no overlap).

ui_bugs.issue: Real mouse clicks on the Back button are intercepted by <input class='hn-nav__toggle' id='hn-nav-toggle'> which is stacked on top of the button at its click coords. document.elementFromPoint returns the INPUT, not the button. Programmatic btn.click() works and correctly calls navigate(-1) (URL changes to previous page and popstate fires), but a genuine user mouse click does nothing. Home link is unaffected. Reproduce: goto /communities-next, SPA-navigate via nav to /luxury-next, click [data-testid='hn-nav-back'] with mouse — URL stays on /luxury-next. This affects all -next pages using the shared nav.

action_items: Fix pointer-event / z-index of .hn-nav__toggle so it does not overlay the .hn-nav__jump / Back button on desktop (and only overlays the burger label as intended). Options: give .hn-nav__toggle a small width/height matching only the burger label area, or add pointer-events:none when not intended as burger-toggle overlay on that region, or reposition it (e.g., position it precisely over the burger label rather than the whole nav).
critical_code_review_comments: The checkbox-hack burger pattern (input.hn-nav__toggle + label.hn-nav__burger) typically uses position:absolute inset:0 or similar which stretches over the header. Even hidden (opacity:0) it still captures pointer events. Confirm CSS constrains hit area to just the burger icon or is display:none on desktop breakpoints.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Verified: Back+Home render on all 4 -next pages LEFT of the EZtoFind logo, with correct labels on desktop and icon-only on mobile 390px (no horizontal overflow, history.length increments correctly). Home link click navigates to '/'. The programmatic btn.click() on Back does call navigate(-1) successfully (popstate fired, URL -> previous), so the React handler is wired correctly. The failure is purely a CSS stacking issue where input#hn-nav-toggle intercepts pointer events over the Back button on desktop. Home is unaffected because its click bubbles from inner SPAN into the parent A tag inside the same stacking context; Back BUTTON at exact centroid gets the INPUT as the topmost hit target.
rca of the issue: elementsFromPoint at Back button centroid on desktop returns: [INPUT.hn-nav__toggle, SPAN, BUTTON.hn-nav__jumpbtn(hn-nav-back), DIV.hn-nav__jump, ...]. The mobile burger toggle checkbox (id=hn-nav-toggle) is stretched over the nav and receives clicks. Mitigation: constrain size/position of .hn-nav__toggle to only the burger icon region, or set display:none / pointer-events:none for viewports >=641px in /app/frontend/src/components/homenext/homeNext.css.
